domain_guidance.summary: Strategic Management focuses on aligning nursing initiatives with organizational vision, developing long‑term plans, and evaluating outcomes to drive improvement. Candidates must understand environmental analysis, change leadership, and the role of nursing executives in shaping health policy.

Financial Management assesses the ability to oversee budgets, interpret financial statements, and allocate resources effectively. Test‑takers need competence in cost‑benefit analysis, revenue cycle oversight, and fiscal decision‑making that supports nursing operations.

Human Resource Management covers workforce planning, talent acquisition, performance evaluation, and staff development. Candidates should master strategies for building high‑performing teams, managing labor relations, and fostering a culture of continuous learning.

Technology Management evaluates proficiency with health‑information systems, data analytics, and emerging digital tools that improve patient care. Examinees must understand implementation, cybersecurity basics, and how technology supports strategic nursing objectives.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early, bring a valid photo ID and your registration confirmation. Bring only approved calculators if needed; the exam is computer‑based and linear, so you cannot return to previous questions. Manage time to answer all 175 items within the 210‑minute window.

faq.answer_text: The NEA‑BC exam contains 175 multiple‑choice questions presented in a linear format. All items must be answered in the order they appear, and you cannot return to earlier questions once you advance.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: A scaled score of 350 on the 200‑to‑500 range is required to pass. Scores below 350 are considered failing, while scores above indicate varying levels of proficiency.
The exam lasts 210 minutes, giving you just over three hours to complete all 175 items. Manage your time carefully to ensure you answer each question within the allotted period.
Non‑members pay $520 for the NEA‑BC exam, while ANA members receive a reduced price of $395. Prices are listed in the ANCC exam guide and must be paid at registration.
faq.question_title: What is the cost for non‑members?

editorial.meta_description: Earn the Nurse Executive Advanced credential. The NEA-BC exam tests strategic, financial, human‑resource and technology management for nursing leaders.

methodology.summary: Content was assembled by extracting verified facts from ANCC official guides and cross‑referencing the exam handbook, renewal requirements, and certification landing page. Domain summaries were written from the listed domain names.

editorial.overview: The Nurse Executive Advanced, Board Certified (NEA-BC) exam, administered by the ANCC, validates senior nursing leaders’ expertise in strategic, financial, human‑resource, and technology management. It consists of 175 multiple‑choice items delivered in a linear format over 210 minutes. Candidates must achieve a scaled score of 350 (on a 200‑500 scale) to earn the five‑year certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the ANCC handbook to understand exam format and content areas. Build a study schedule that allocates time to each of the four domains, using current nursing leadership literature and the IOM report on education transformation. Practice with multiple‑choice questions, focusing on scenario‑based items that reflect strategic, financial, HR, and technology decisions. Join a peer study group or online forum for discussion and feedback. Take at least one full‑length practice test under timed conditions.
editorial.who_should_take: Current nurse executives, directors of nursing, chief nursing officers, and senior managers with at least several years of leadership experience should pursue NEA‑BC to demonstrate advanced executive competence in healthcare.

exam_rules: Closed-book. No notes or reference materials permitted. On-screen calculator provided where applicable. 60-day waiting period required before retaking. MSN or APRN graduate degree required for advanced practice NP certifications.
id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. Name must match ANCC registration exactly. RN license number required at check-in.

prerequisites.description: Current, active RN license in the US or its territories
Master's degree or higher in nursing or related field
24 months experience at the senior executive level of nursing administration

renewal_options: Earn 75 CE credits (contact hours) every 5 years. CE credits must be relevant to the certification specialty. Submit renewal application via the ANCC certification portal. Maintain current, active RN license throughout certification period.

retake_policy.notes: Must wait 60 days before retaking. Full exam fee required for each retake attempt. Check ANCC website for current retake policies.

testing_centers.notes: Computer-based testing at Prometric test centers; online proctoring available for select exams
